question: Does a minimal span-wise dual-lane decoder module recover buried microphone content through the deployed endpoint, serial-worker, merge, and identity semantics without worsening the measured live latency or bounded lifecycle?
scope: Prototype only. The inputs are synthetic 15.377 dB lane disparities. Even a passing result requires fresh real attended evidence before production use.

module_interface.input: One frozen span plus aligned system and microphone PCM for exactly that span.
module_interface.output: One merged timed transcript, per-lane source trace, aggregate decode diagnostics, and lane-specific PCM ownership for every local speaker.
invariants: At most one bounded arbiter item per frozen span.
Within that item, active lanes decode serially; no second worker or fairness bypass.
Local speaker labels are namespaced by lane before stable time ordering.
Overlaps are preserved; no clipping, deduplication, or forced turn order.
Identity embeds each local speaker only from the PCM lane that produced it.

measurements.endpoint: Production WebRTC provider and EndpointPolicy over production mono-mix frames.
measurements.decode: Production VllmRunner and canonical token cap; retain raw transcript, parsed segments, elapsed time, tokens, capped and parse classification.
measurements.content: Sealed v3 shuffle-edit score against both clean lane references.
measurements.identity: Production WeSpeaker embeddings from the owning lane, replayed through accepted album plus terminal sweep with lane identity as truth.
measurements.latency: Single-worker queue from actual span freeze times and decode durations, plus the bound active-reader render time.
measurements.lifecycle: Queue depth, final stop-drain tail, two-session round-robin item fairness, request multiplier, and speaker capacity.
measurements.structure: Parse roundtrip, segment preservation, collision-free lane namespace, overlap preservation, and source trace.

decision_rule.content: Dual-lane WER improves by at least 0.05 absolute on all four corpora.
decision_rule.structure: Every corpus preserves all parsed source segments, roundtrips, preserves overlaps, and stays within 16 speakers.
decision_rule.identity: At least 0.80 duration-weighted accuracy, at most 4 canonical speakers, and no embedding failures on every corpus.
decision_rule.decode_integrity: No capped, empty, or unparseable lane decode on any corpus.
decision_rule.bounded_lifecycle: Max queue depth at most 16, stop drain at most 5 s, exactly 2x requests, and two-session maximum service skew at most one completed span while both sessions have work.
decision_rule.latency: Dual-lane first-word and last-word p95 must not exceed same-span mono baseline on any corpus. Attribution already proved span accumulation dominates; a microphone remedy cannot consume the latency improvement the active goal requires.
